title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript page. It is the recto of a reused sheet: a typed, upside-down examination paper from the Université des Sciences et Techniques du Languedoc (Montpellier), June 1978 session, for the certificate 'C4 Mathématiques Pures et Approfondies, Option de M. Petrich'. The question reads: 'Describe the conjugacy classes of subgroups and of elements of the alternating group A5, giving their geometric interpretation in terms of the icosahedron.' Grothendieck used the back of the sheet for his notes, which appear as page 72. There he works with the line bundles L_i, L_A, L on M_{0,I} and the sections xi_A, with nu=(n-1)(n-2)/2. The faint mirror-image handwriting visible here is that verso bleeding through. It is not new content.

Standard answer to the exam question. A5 is the rotation group of the icosahedron, of order 60.
- Element classes: identity (1).
- 15 involutions: half-turns about the 15 axes through midpoints of opposite edges (30 edges).
- 20 elements of order 3: rotations by ±2π/3 about the 10 axes through centres of opposite faces (20 faces).
- Two classes of 12 elements of order 5: rotations by ±2π/5 and by ±4π/5 about the 6 vertex axes (12 vertices). These classes are swapped by the outer automorphism of S5, i.e. by conjugation by a transposition, which induces the Galois conjugation √5 ↦ -√5 of the golden ratio.
- Subgroup classes (9 in total): 1; C2 (15); C3 (10); V4 (5), the three mutually perpendicular edge-axes of each of the 5 inscribed octahedra or cubes; C5 (6); S3 = D3 (10), stabilisers of a face-axis; D5 (6), stabilisers of a vertex-axis; A4 (5), stabilisers of the 5 inscribed octahedra (equivalently the 5 cubes or 5 tetrahedra in the dual dodecahedron); A5 itself.
- The action on the 5 inscribed octahedra realises A5 inside S5.

Relevance to the neighbouring notes: the notes concern M_{0,n} and n=5, where S5 = Aut(M_{0,5}). The presence of the A5/icosahedron exam is very likely just scrap paper. At most it is a coincidental thematic echo of Grothendieck's later interest in regular polyhedra and dessins.

ideas.what: Conjugacy classes of elements and subgroups of A5 interpreted via rotations of the icosahedron (an exam question, not by Grothendieck)
ideas.modern_name: Icosahedral rotation group A5 and its subgroup lattice
ideas.where_published: Standard textbook material; Grothendieck discusses regular polyhedra and dessins in Esquisse d'un programme, but not this exercise

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typed 1978 Montpellier exam sheet reused as scrap paper. It has no Grothendieck mathematics on it. The handwriting showing through belongs to the verso, transcribed as page 72.
